fixture_name: Four-lane arterial improvement — US preliminary design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Queuing/turning/parking interference at closely-spaced intersections on a corridor with recorded high-accident designations is a substantive preliminary-design safety concern.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim is backed by a verbatim EV-US-016 quote matching the concern text, with supplementary location detail attributed to recorded case-study input (TABLE A.1 Issue 3).
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a categorical safety_concern with no compliance conflation, appropriate to FHWA preliminary-design stage semantics.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and viable design-stage actions (turning restrictions plus relocating parking stalls outside the intersection functional area); minor looseness in 'specified' stalls does not defeat actionability.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists explicitly acknowledged along the commercial corridor, though the vehicle-vehicle conflict mechanism makes direct VRU analysis not applicable here.

justifications.substance: Queue spillback between signals only 650 ft apart on a high-accident corridor is a substantive preliminary-design safety issue affecting intersection operation and crash risk.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal 650-ft spacing claim is supported by a verbatim quote from EV-US-001, and the derived spillback inference is transparently labeled rather than invented.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a safety concern under FHWA RSA practice for closely spaced signals, with no conflation into a compliance determination.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Recommendation is specific and actionable (signal coordination, Do Not Block Intersection signing, enhanced conspicuity) and viable at preliminary design stage.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists are explicitly acknowledged with a reasoned scoping to vehicle occupants for this mechanism, matching the not-applicable-but-acknowledged case.
